## TL;DR

Release emails are in place for any project with `[auth.emailProvider]` set up. When `[release.email]` is enabled, a stable cut sends each recipient one email with the version, notes, the known issues typed in the release modal, and links. By default it waits until GitHub serves the release with its assets. The Releases page shows the send state with Preview and Resend. The scoped `repoos check` passed (exit 0, 7,446 test results, none failing). Three acceptance items are not done: the bell notice for failed sends, a "send test email" action, and a dedicated CLI subcommand. They are listed below.

## Work and rationale

**Shared sender.** Resend calls lived inside `routes/auth.ts`. I moved them to `src/server/email.ts` so login codes, invites and release emails share one path. `sendEmail` never throws; it returns a reason the caller can record. `buildFromHeader` is re-exported from auth because a test imports it from there.

**Config.** `[release.email]` has four keys: `enabled`, `to`, `when` and `includePrereleases`. All default to off or to the safe choice. `parseReleaseEmailConfig` drops invalid addresses with a warning and falls back to `published` for an unknown `when`. The keys are in `SUPPORTED_TOML_KEYS`, `getConfigSchema()` and `user-docs/configuration.md`. The Settings PATCH needed a dedicated `release.email.to` branch, because the generic array branch rejects empty lists, and an empty recipient list is the normal state.

**Settings.** I added a `release-emails` General section. Its four rows render from the schema, so no hand-written markup was needed.

**Renderer and send logic.** `src/server/release-email.ts` holds the renderer, publish detection and the send record. Every user-supplied string is HTML-escaped before any markup is added. Notes and known issues go through a small markdown subset that only links http and https. The text alternative keeps the same structure. Empty notes render "No release notes were written"; empty known issues render "None recorded".

**Publish detection.** A `published` send with a repository polls the public releases-by-tag API with plain `fetch`. A release counts as published when it is not a draft and has at least one asset. The first probe is immediate. A network error on that first probe means "unavailable", and the email goes at the tag with a reason recorded. Later probes back off to three minutes and stop after an hour, recording a failure that asks the human to resend.

**Idempotency.** `.repoos/release-emails.json` holds one record per version: status, `sentTo`, reason, `when` and time. A `sent` record makes the automatic path a no-op. An in-flight set stops one cut from running twice. A malformed file throws instead of reading as empty. An empty read would make a sent release look unsent and cause a second send. Resend targets only configured recipients who are not in `sentTo`, so a partial failure can be retried without mailing anyone twice.

**Cut hook.** `cutNewRelease` takes an optional `knownIssues` argument, stores it on the release entry, and calls `startCutReleaseEmail` after the tag push. The call is detached and the release outcome does not depend on it.

**Routes and UI.** Three routes: status, preview, and explicit send. `POST /api/release` now accepts `knownIssues`. The Releases page has a known-issues field in the cut form and a release-email card. The card shows sent, pending, failed or skipped, with Preview and a confirmed Resend. It polls every 30 seconds while a send is pending.

**Docs.** `user-docs/configuration.md` has a Release emails section with a key table. `docs/releases.md` covers the design, the record, the API rows and the known gaps.

## Approaches tried

- **Git hook versus publish detection.** I chose the API poll the task specifies. A hook fires before CI has built anything, so the email would announce a version with no download.
- **Where to store the sent record.** I considered putting it in the committed `release-history.json`. That would make every send a repository change. I used a gitignored per-version file under `cacheDir` instead.
- **Resend scope.** Resend could resend to everyone or only to the people who missed it. I chose the latter, so a retry never mails someone twice. The button only sends to recipients who do not yet have the email.
- **Test seams.** The publish wait takes an injected sleep, clock and fetch. The tests run with no real network or mail.
- **Test location.** My first test file went under `src/server/__tests__`, which the vitest include (`tests/**/*.test.ts`) does not pick up. I moved it to `src/ui-app/tests/release-email.test.ts`, where the rest of the suite runs.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Bell notice not done.** Acceptance item 3 asks for a bell notice on failure. The attention feed needs a new kind across `core/attention.ts`, the server feed plumbing, and the notices and notifications stores. I did not build it in this pass. The docs list it as a gap.
- **No "send test email".** Acceptance item 2 mentions one. I built the Preview, which renders without sending. A send-to-self test needs a decision about who the test goes to, so I left it out.
- **No dedicated CLI.** `POST` routes under `/api/release` are covered by the existing parity exemption. The preview is available through the HTTP route; there is no `repoos release email` subcommand.
- **Restart during the wait.** A process restart during the publish wait leaves the record `pending`. The card shows that state, and Resend recovers it. The wait does not resume automatically.
- **Scoped check wait.** My first `repoos check` run was killed at the background limit while queued behind remote validation. I restarted it with the maximum limit. The restarted run finished green.
- **Edit-tool notices.** The edit tool reported several files as changed on disk during the session. I re-read the changed files and confirmed my edits were intact before continuing.

## Key learnings

- The vitest include is `tests/**/*.test.ts` under `src/ui-app`. Tests placed elsewhere silently never run.
- The Settings PATCH validates each schema field by type. A new array key with a "non-empty" guard will reject every ordinary save once the list is empty, so it needs its own branch.
- Parsing a key alone does not make it effective. `[release.email]` only applies when `[release] enabled` is true, because `loadConfig` only sets `cfg.release` in that case. The Settings description says so.
- A record that can be wrong about "already sent" is worse than one that can be stale. A malformed log must fail closed, so the code throws rather than reading empty.
